title: Module constants _VARIABLE_WIDTH_COLUMN_BYTES and _UNKNOWN_WIDTH_COLUMN_BYTES are defined but never referenced
description: Lines 201-202 define `_VARIABLE_WIDTH_COLUMN_BYTES = 64` and `_UNKNOWN_WIDTH_COLUMN_BYTES = 64`. Neither name is used anywhere in the module or the test suite. The byte-budget width estimation path uses `_DEFAULT_PROJECTED_COLUMN_BYTES` (line 180, also 64) for both the unknown-column fallback in `_estimate_projected_row_bytes` (line 649) and the unmapped-dtype fallback in `_dtype_estimated_width` (line 691). These two constants are leftover scaffolding from an apparently abandoned width-classification design (variable-width vs unknown-width) that was never wired up. They also silently duplicate the value 64 three ways, creating drift risk if someone later edits one but not the others.
evidence: Grep across the entire repo (`src/haute` and `tests`) for `_VARIABLE_WIDTH_COLUMN_BYTES` / `_UNKNOWN_WIDTH_COLUMN_BYTES` returns matches ONLY at the definition site src/haute/chunking.py:201-202 (one file, two lines, the definitions themselves). By contrast `_DEFAULT_PROJECTED_COLUMN_BYTES` is referenced at lines 649 and 691. The width-estimation functions (`_estimate_projected_row_bytes` 629-651, `_dtype_estimated_width` 690-691) never read the two constants.
est_reduction: -2 LOC (delete the two unused constants); removes a 3-way duplicated literal/drift hazard
behavior_preservation: The constants are never read by any code path, so deleting them cannot change behavior. `_estimate_projected_row_bytes` and `_dtype_estimated_width` continue to use `_DEFAULT_PROJECTED_COLUMN_BYTES` unchanged.
